bib.title: GSM-Symbolic: Understanding the Limitations of Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models

read.skipped: Reference list (about 18000 chars) skimmed only for lineage

question: Are reported GSM8K scores reliable measures of mathematical reasoning, and how robust is LLM reasoning to changed names, numbers, difficulty and irrelevant clauses?
hypothesis: LLMs do not perform formal reasoning but in-distribution pattern matching, so accuracy should vary across instantiations of one question and collapse under added clauses or irrelevant information.
contributions: GSM-Symbolic: a template-based generator of GSM8K variants
Evidence that GSM8K accuracy is a distribution with variance and a drop on GSM-Symbolic, hinting at contamination
Models are robust to name changes but sensitive to number changes; accuracy falls and variance rises with clause count
GSM-NoOp: irrelevant but plausible clauses cause drops of up to 65%

method.summary: The authors hand-annotate 100 GSM8K test questions as symbolic templates (variables, domains, conditions), generate 50 instances of each, and evaluate 25 open and closed models 8-shot with CoT and greedy decoding. Variants change names only, numbers only, remove/add 1-2 clauses (M1, P1, P2) or add an irrelevant clause (NoOp).
method.task: grade-school math word problems, robustness evaluation

datasets.name: GSM8K
datasets.split: test; also a random subset of 100 test questions used as templates

datasets.name: GSM-Symbolic (and Names, M1, P1, P2, NoOp variants)
datasets.size: 100 templates x 50 samples = 5000 examples per benchmark (50 datasets of 100)
datasets.split: derived from 100 random GSM8K test questions
datasets.preprocessing: Templates annotated by hand; automated checks that original values do not appear, original values satisfy conditions, answer matches; 10 random samples per template manually reviewed; questions that fewer than two models answer correctly are re-reviewed manually. Numeric ranges kept close to GSM8K, slightly widened.

datasets.name: GSM-P1 fine-tuning set
datasets.size: 10000 examples generated from 50 P1 templates separate from test templates

models.name: Gemma, Gemma2 (2b, 7b, 2b, 9b, 27b; base and it), Phi-2, Phi-3 (mini, small, medium), Phi-3.5-mini, Mistral-7b (v0.1, v0.3; base and instruct), Mathstral-7b-v0.1, Llama3-8b (base and instruct)

inference.decoding: greedy for all models except o1-mini and o1-preview (API does not allow control; responses to the same prompt change)
inference.max_tokens: generation until context limit, end-of-response token, or the model begins the next 'Q:'
inference.samples: one greedy run per model per 100-question set, 50 sets per benchmark; nearly 500 total evaluations
inference.prompting: 8-shot chain of thought with the original 8 GSM8K shots (except NoOp-Symb and NoOp-NoOp experiments, and P1-shot ablation); preamble 'As an expert problem solver, solve step by step the following mathematical questions.'

other.shots_ablation: preliminary experiments said shot count did not significantly change performance; no numbers given

metrics.name: accuracy
metrics.definition: fraction of the 100 questions in a set answered correctly; reported as mean (+- value) over 50 sets

metrics.name: arithmetic accuracy
metrics.definition: Gemma2-9b-it and Phi-3-medium zero-shot 'What is x plus y?' with at least 1000 cases per digit length and operation; plus equations extracted from responses

baselines: GSM8K subset of the 100 template questions
eval.protocol: One-sample two-sided t-test of the 50 GSM-Symbolic scores against the GSM8K(100) score (normality tested); authors say a two-sample z-test (Ivanova et al. 2025) would give non-significant results.

evidence.quote: we calculate statistical significance using the one-sample t-test with two-sided alternative hypothesis

limits: The +- in all tables is undefined (probably std over 50 sets); each set holds only 100 questions, so per-set noise is large and the best-worst gap is of the size sampling alone produces (the paper itself concedes that under Ivanova et al. 2025's two-sample test the drops are non-significant).
Only 100 templates, hand-annotated; base GSM8K comparison is a single score on the same 100 questions.
o1 models not decoded greedily; no seeds or repeated runs per set; decoding and context lengths per model not given.
Contamination explanation is a hypothesis; no direct check of training data.
Authors concede they should have articulated statistical assumptions more clearly, and argue a 'true reasoner' would give a degenerate distribution (App B).
Fine-tuning ablation reports only Phi-3.5 and gives no optimizer or lr.
Models are 2024 vintage; o1-preview, the strongest, lost only 17.5 on NoOp.
